answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit locked behind a slow, verifiable work history, like a yarrow root that only grows deep with time. New identities start with a tiny trust budget and must earn reputation through completed, peer-reviewed tasks before they can bridge into high-value exchanges. One verified credential, a pearl earned once and hard to fake, anchors each agent's history, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs far more than any one of them can earn.
